A bottleneck occurs when one component (CPU or GPU) is much stronger than the other, limiting overall performance.
If your CPU is weak but GPU is strong, the CPU 'bottlenecks' and wastes your GPU's power. Balance is key!
Bottlenecking means one part of your PC is holding back the other. For example, a weak GPU with a strong CPU.
Think of it like a water bottle - even if the bottle is huge, if the neck is tiny, water flows slowly. Same with PC parts!
A bottleneck happens when your CPU and GPU aren't balanced, preventing you from getting maximum FPS.
To minimize bottlenecks, match your CPU and GPU performance levels for the best gaming experience!
Lower your resolution for more FPS! Or reduce graphics settings and disable ray tracing.
Close background apps, update drivers, and lower your resolution or graphics settings to boost FPS.
Best FPS tips: Lower resolution → reduce graphics details → close background programs → update GPU drivers.
Try these: disable V-sync, lower shadow quality, reduce draw distance, and cap frame rate to your monitor's refresh rate.
Optimize by turning off anti-aliasing, lowering texture quality, disabling bloom, and closing unnecessary background applications.
For better performance: use high-performance power settings, clean dust from your PC, and consider overclocking!
FPS stands for Frames Per Second — it measures how many images your PC renders every second. Higher FPS = smoother gameplay! 🎮
FPS (Frames Per Second) is how many frames your GPU renders each second. 60 FPS is smooth, 144 FPS is competitive, 240+ FPS is ultra-smooth!
Think of FPS like a flipbook — the more pages (frames) per second, the smoother the animation. More FPS = smoother gaming experience!
FPS measures your game's smoothness. Below 30 FPS feels laggy, 60 FPS is comfortable, 144+ FPS is ideal for competitive gaming!
Frames Per Second (FPS) = how many images your screen shows per second. Higher FPS means less blur and faster response — crucial for competitive games like Valorant or CS2!
